headline: Charlotte is a forgotten recording town (WBT, the 1936 Bluebird sessions, James Brown's 'Brand New Bag') with a Hive-era hip-hop-soul memory and a quietly deep rap bench, a soundtrack the post-LaMelo Hornets have room to claim with Nike as co-author.
summary: Charlotte's music story is mostly untold: WBT (1922) and RCA's 1936-38 Bluebird field sessions made it an early country-recording hub, and James Brown cut 'Papa's Got a Brand New Bag' at Arthur Smith's Charlotte studio in 1965. The team's golden memory, the teal-and-purple Hive that sold out 364 straight games, is the same early-90s moment Charlotte's Jodeci defined hip-hop soul, while today's rap scene runs from DaBaby's chart power (and baggage) to critics' picks Lute, MAVI and Reuben Vincent. The West End's HBCU band culture at Johnson C. Smith, the CIAA's old February takeover, Petey Pablo's statewide anthem 'Raise Up' and a two-state roots-and-country base (the Avett Brothers, Luke Combs, Earl Scruggs) complete the picture. With LaMelo Ball traded to Minnesota and Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel now the faces, Nike's lane is a 'Cut in Charlotte' sound and visual language built with paid local partners, not borrowed hip-hop clichés from other cities.

insights.title: Charlotte cut records before Nashville did
insights.detail: WBT signed on in 1922 and its Briarhoppers string band ruled 1930s Carolina radio; RCA's Bluebird label ran field sessions in Uptown in 1936-38, where the Monroe Brothers made their first records. Arthur Smith's 'Guitar Boogie' and 'Feudin' Banjos' (later 'Dueling Banjos') came out of Charlotte, and James Brown recorded 'Papa's Got a Brand New Bag' at Arthur Smith Studios in 1965.
insights.implication: A 'Cut in Charlotte' story (liner notes, 78-rpm label type, radio-dial graphics) gives City product heritage no other NBA market has and few locals know, provided artist names, recordings and label marks are licensed.

insights.title: The Hive and hip-hop soul are one memory
insights.detail: The Hornets sold out 364 straight games at the 24,000-seat Charlotte Coliseum as Larry Johnson and Alonzo Mourning arrived in 1991-92, the same moment Charlotte's Jodeci released 'Forever My Lady' and helped invent hip-hop soul. Charlotte-born Anthony Hamilton carried that lineage into the 2000s with 'Comin' from Where I'm From'.
insights.implication: Teal throwback product should sound like early-90s Charlotte R&B, not generic 90s nostalgia: soundtrack it with Hamilton or a licensed Jodeci moment and aim it at the 35-50-year-old fans who wore the Starter jackets the first time.

insights.title: Rap's biggest local name carries baggage; the credible bench is deep
insights.detail: DaBaby, raised in Charlotte, landed a No. 1 album ('Kirk', 2019) and No. 1 single ('Rockstar', 2020) but lost festival slots after homophobic remarks at Rolling Loud in 2021. Lute (J. Cole's Dreamville; 'West1996', 'Gold Mouf'), MAVI ('Let the Sun Talk') and Reuben Vincent (9th Wonder's Jamla) are the respected local voices.
insights.implication: Build artist collaborations, credited and paid, with Lute, MAVI or Reuben Vincent and keep DaBaby out of any lead role; in a city that lost the 2017 All-Star Game over the HB2 'bathroom bill', inclusion is not optional.

insights.title: The West End's sound is brass and drums
insights.detail: Johnson C. Smith University on Beatties Ford Road fields the International Institute of Sound marching band, and from 2006 to 2020 the CIAA Tournament filled Charlotte's arena and clubs each February with step shows and concerts before moving to Baltimore. Up the road, the 1944 Excelsior Club hosted touring Black stars until it closed in 2016.
insights.implication: Co-design an HBCU-night or CIAA-week capsule with JCSU (band braid, drumhead graphics, navy and gold), pay the band and route proceeds to its music program; the look should come from the band, not be costumed by Nike.

insights.title: 'Raise Up' is the state's crowd ritual
insights.detail: Greenville rapper Petey Pablo's 2001 'Raise Up' ('North Carolina, come on and raise up... spin it like a helicopter') is still the shirt-twirling anthem at Carolinas stadiums. Coby White, from Goldsboro in eastern NC and a former Tar Heel, re-signed this summer as part of the new core.
insights.implication: A helicopter rally towel or twist-to-read tee built on the 'raise up' gesture, fronted by a homegrown player like White if he is a Nike athlete and cleared with the song's rights holders, is a crowd ritual Nike can own.

insights.title: The team's soundtrack is up for grabs
insights.detail: Charlotte's 2019 NBA All-Star Game put Carolinas artists on the Spectrum Center floor (performer lineup to be confirmed), and Fayetteville's J. Cole and Charlotte's Anthony Hamilton are the state's best-known voices. The LaMelo Ball era and its Puma-driven content are now over, and the team belongs to Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel.
insights.implication: Commission a Charlotte producer and a local artist-in-residence for intros, hype videos and drop soundtracks during the reset, after confirming which player faces are not contracted to rival brands (Miller has been a Puma athlete).

insights.title: The Carolinas gave jazz its giants
insights.detail: John Coltrane (Hamlet, NC), Thelonious Monk (Rocky Mount), Dizzy Gillespie (Cheraw, SC) and Nina Simone (Tryon, NC) were all born inside the Hornets' two-state territory. Charlotte-born Romare Bearden made jazz and blues the subject of collages such as his 'Of the Blues' series, and Uptown's Romare Bearden Park carries his name.
insights.implication: A Bearden-licensed collage graphic or a 'Carolinas jazz' story supports a premium, adult capsule with real roots; work through the Romare Bearden Foundation and the musicians' estates rather than imitating the style.

places.name: Neighborhood Theatre
places.why: A converted neighborhood movie house at the center of the NoDa arts district and the mid-size room local acts graduate to.

places.name: Snug Harbor
places.why: A pirate-themed dive where indie bands, dance nights and drag share a stage: where Plaza Midwood's scene actually hangs out.

places.name: Lunchbox Records
places.why: The independent vinyl shop that carries local releases, a natural pickup point for a numbered, record-style product drop.

places.name: The Milestone Club
places.why: A punk dive open since 1969 where R.E.M. played early shows; the city's DIY credential.

places.name: Visulite Theatre
places.why: An intimate room in a historic storefront theater, a reliable stop for touring and Carolinas acts since 1999.

places.name: The Fillmore Charlotte at AvidXchange Music Factory
places.why: The main mid-size touring hub, sharing a campus with The Underground and Skyla Credit Union Amphitheatre.

places.name: Johnson C. Smith University
places.why: Home of the International Institute of Sound band and anchor of the Beatties Ford corridor's Black music heritage.

places.name: Camp North End
places.why: A 1924 Ford assembly plant turned arts, food and music campus where Charlotte's younger creative scene gathers; a good launch site.

places.name: Romare Bearden Park
places.why: Named for the Charlotte-born collage artist whose work is steeped in jazz and blues; a short walk from Spectrum Center.

places.name: Earl Scruggs Center
places.why: Honors the banjo innovator from nearby Flint Hill and roots the Hornets' wider-Carolinas fan base in bluegrass history.

people.name: Anthony Hamilton
people.role: Charlotte-born soul singer ('Charlene', 'Comin' from Where I'm From')
people.why: The most respected living voice of Charlotte R&B and the natural lead for any Hive-era or anthem-night campaign.

people.name: Jodeci
people.role: Charlotte R&B quartet (K-Ci, JoJo, DeVante Swing, Mr. Dalvin)
people.why: Defined early-90s hip-hop soul during the Hornets' sellout run; their name, likeness and recordings need licensing.

people.name: Lute
people.role: West Charlotte rapper signed to J. Cole's Dreamville
people.why: Raps about Charlotte's West Side with Dreamville credibility, a strong fit for a credited local collab.

people.name: MAVI
people.role: Charlotte rapper ('Let the Sun Talk', 'Laughing So Hard, It Hurts')
people.why: A critics' favorite with literary, hometown-rooted lyrics, the rising voice younger Charlotte fans rep.

people.name: DaBaby
people.role: Charlotte-raised rapper; founder of Billion Dollar Baby Entertainment
people.why: The city's biggest commercial rap star and a reputational risk since 2021; know him, but do not build around him.

people.name: International Institute of Sound (JCSU)
people.role: Johnson C. Smith University marching band
people.why: The West End's living HBCU band tradition and the obvious paid partner for a drumline, band-braid or CIAA-week activation.

people.name: Arthur Smith (1921-2014)
people.role: Guitarist, TV host and studio owner ('Guitar Boogie', 'Feudin' Banjos')
people.why: Turned Charlotte into a recording hub; James Brown cut 'Papa's Got a Brand New Bag' in his studio.

people.name: Luke Combs
people.role: Country star born in Huntersville and raised in Asheville
people.why: Co-headlined the October 2024 Concert for Carolina for Helene relief with Eric Church, the face of the region's country audience alongside Concord's Avett Brothers.

moments.name: Hornets home opener
moments.why: The first Spectrum Center night of the Miller-Knueppel era, the moment to debut a new game-night sound and a music-led drop.

moments.name: JCSU Homecoming
moments.why: The International Institute of Sound's biggest showcase on Beatties Ford Road and a West End gathering for alumni.

moments.name: CIAA Tournament week
moments.why: Charlotte's Black music and party week from 2006 to 2020; whether it returns or not, it is the template for an HBCU basketball-and-music night.

moments.name: MerleFest
moments.why: The Carolinas' flagship roots festival since 1988, named for Doc Watson's son Merle, reaching western-NC Hornets fans.

moments.name: Charlotte Pride Festival & Parade
moments.why: Uptown's largest summer street festival; after HB2, visible and credited inclusion work matters here.

moments.name: Festival in the Park
moments.why: A neighborhood arts-and-music festival running since 1964, a low-key preseason window to seed product with local makers.

vocabulary.meaning: The Hornets' rallying name for the team and city since the Hornets name returned in 2014.
The old Charlotte Coliseum of the 1988-2002 sellout years, now used for any loud Hornets crowd.
Charlotte's nickname, after Queen Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz; the crown motif comes from it.
Charlotte's area code, repped by local rappers and on merch (980 is the overlay).
What Charlotteans call downtown, home of Spectrum Center; saying 'downtown' marks an outsider.
Petey Pablo's 2001 NC anthem, and the cue to twist your shirt around your head and spin it like a helicopter.
The Carolinas' swing dance to beach music; South Carolina's state dance and North Carolina's official popular dance.
Carolinas shorthand for the R&B and soul records played at coastal pavilions and shag clubs, not surf rock.

designCues.cue: Hornets teal as the hero color for anything Hive-era or hip-hop-soul, paired with Hornets purple #1D1160
designCues.source: The 1988 palette by North Carolina designer Alexander Julian; the color of the sold-out Hive and early-90s Charlotte R&B
designCues.use: Lead throwback and R&B-campaign product with teal and purple; team colors and marks run through NBA Properties.

designCues.source: JCSU's navy-and-gold International Institute of Sound uniforms on Beatties Ford Road
designCues.use: Use for soutache-style trim and drumhead roundels on a JCSU co-designed capsule; treat the hex as a working value and match JCSU's official gold.

designCues.cue: Cut-paper collage layering with torn edges and flat color blocks
designCues.source: Charlotte-born Romare Bearden's jazz and blues collages, such as the 'Of the Blues' series
designCues.use: License through the Romare Bearden Foundation or commission Charlotte collage artists for a layered shooting-shirt print; never trace or mimic Bearden's compositions.

designCues.cue: 1930s radio and 78-rpm label lettering: condensed deco caps, dial arcs, a circular 'label' neck print
designCues.source: WBT's early broadcast era and the 1936-38 Bluebird sessions in Uptown
designCues.use: Draw original lettering for a 'Cut in Charlotte' collection; avoid the RCA and Bluebird marks, which belong to a major label.

designCues.cue: Liner-notes tracklist back print: 'Recorded in Charlotte, NC' with years and credits
designCues.source: Charlotte's recording timeline: Monroe Brothers (1936), 'Guitar Boogie', 'Papa's Got a Brand New Bag' (1965), Jodeci (1991)
designCues.use: Set as a tracklist on a warmup back or hang-tag booklet; clear every artist name and song title with rights holders first.

designCues.cue: Oversized early-90s hip-hop-soul silhouette: drop shoulders, boxy satin and nylon, baggy shorts
designCues.source: Jodeci-era Charlotte R&B styling (oversized denim, leather, combat boots, backwards caps) during the Hive's sellout run
designCues.use: Reference the era, not the group's likeness, in teal-and-purple warmup jackets; use the group only under license.

designCues.cue: Helicopter-spin graphic printed to read when the shirt is twisted around the head
designCues.source: The 'Raise Up' stadium ritual across North Carolina
designCues.use: Rally towels and giveaway tees; partner with and pay Petey Pablo rather than printing the lyric unlicensed.

productHooks: 'Cut in Charlotte' City capsule: a warmup jacket and shooting shirt with a liner-notes back print and 78-label neck graphic, sold as a numbered run through Lunchbox Records with a 7-inch or playlist from Lute, MAVI or Reuben Vincent, launched at the Neighborhood Theatre.
HBCU-night or CIAA-week capsule co-designed with JCSU's International Institute of Sound: navy-and-gold band-braid warmups, a drumline pregame, and proceeds to JCSU's music program.

Hive-era R&B throwback drop in teal and purple satin, fronted by Anthony Hamilton (anthem plus campaign) and tied to Converse heritage, since Larry Johnson's 'Grandmama' ads were for Converse, now part of Nike.
'Raise Up' Carolinas Night: helicopter rally towels and twist-to-read tees, led by a homegrown player such as Coby White if he is a Nike athlete, with Petey Pablo paid and cleared.
Premium 'Carolinas Jazz' capsule (collage-print hoodie and knit) licensed from the Romare Bearden Foundation for adult fans, sold at Spectrum Center and Uptown museum shops.
watchouts: DaBaby is Charlotte's biggest commercial rapper, but his 2021 Rolling Loud remarks about gay people and HIV cost him festival slots, and Charlotte lost the 2017 All-Star Game over HB2; no lead role without a full review.
Footwear conflicts: Brandon Miller has been a Puma athlete and LaMelo Ball (now in Minnesota) was Puma; confirm Miller's, Knueppel's and Coby White's deals before any player-artist content.
Licensing: James Brown's and Jodeci's names and recordings, Petey Pablo's 'Raise Up' lyric, Romare Bearden's art, the RCA/Bluebird label marks and all Hornets/NBA marks need clearance.

West End Black music heritage, including the Excelsior Club and the Brooklyn neighborhood razed by 1960s urban renewal, must be told with JCSU, West End groups and the artists themselves, credited and paid, not as nostalgia graphics.
Beach music and the shag grew from Black R&B records played at segregated Carolina beach pavilions; if product touches that nostalgia, credit the Black originators.
